qs.q: Where is your hometown?
qs.model: I’m from Jeddah, which is on the west coast of Saudi Arabia, right on the Red Sea. It’s the second-largest city in the country, and it’s known as the gateway to Makkah.

tip.ar: أجب ثم أضف تفصيلًا أو اثنين. لا تكتفِ باسم المدينة.
tip.en: Answer, then add one or two details. Don’t just name the city.

qs.q: What do you like most about it?
qs.model: Definitely the sea. In the evenings, people go to the Corniche to walk, have a coffee and enjoy the breeze. It’s a really relaxing place to unwind after a busy day.

tip.ar: استخدم كلمة مثل Definitely أو I’d say لتبدو طبيعيًا.
tip.en: Start with “Definitely” or “I’d say” to sound natural.

qs.q: Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
qs.model: Yes, quite a lot. There are many new entertainment venues and restaurants, and the old district, Al-Balad, has been restored beautifully. On the downside, the traffic has got much worse.

tip.ar: سؤال عن التغير: استخدم المضارع التام (has been restored, has got worse).
tip.en: Questions about change: use the present perfect.

qs.q: Would you like to live there in the future?
qs.model: I think so, yes. My family is there and I feel at home. Having said that, I’d like to live abroad for a few years first, maybe while I’m doing my master’s degree.

tip.ar: «Having said that» تضيف رأيًا مقابلًا بطريقة طبيعية.
tip.en: “Having said that” adds a contrasting idea naturally.

qs.q: Do you work or are you a student?
qs.model: I’m a student at the moment. I’m in my final year at university, studying computer engineering, and I’m hoping to do a postgraduate degree abroad next year.

tip.ar: قل ماذا تدرس وفي أي سنة، وأضف خطتك.
tip.en: Say what and which year, and add a plan.

qs.q: Why did you choose that subject?
qs.model: I’ve always been fascinated by how technology works. When I was a teenager, I used to take apart old phones just to see what was inside, so engineering felt like a natural choice.

tip.ar: «used to» لعادات الماضي تعطي الإجابة عمقًا.
tip.en: “Used to” for past habits adds depth.

qs.q: What is the most difficult part of your studies?
qs.model: Probably the workload. We have a lot of projects with tight deadlines, so managing my time is a real challenge, especially near the end of the semester.

tip.ar: استخدم مفردات دقيقة: workload، tight deadlines.
tip.en: Use precise words: workload, tight deadlines.

qs.q: What would you like to do after you graduate?
qs.model: Ideally, I’d like to work for a technology company that builds smart city systems. There are huge projects in Saudi Arabia at the moment, so I think there’ll be great opportunities.

tip.ar: «Ideally, I’d like to…» بداية ممتازة لأسئلة المستقبل.
tip.en: “Ideally, I’d like to…” is a great start for future questions.

qs.q: What do you usually do in your free time?
qs.model: It depends on how much time I have. On weekdays I usually just watch a series or play football with friends, but at weekends I like going out to the desert with my family.

tip.ar: «It depends on…» تفتح الإجابة لتفاصيل أكثر.
tip.en: “It depends on…” opens space for detail.

qs.q: Do you prefer spending free time alone or with others?
qs.model: With others, mostly. I’m quite a sociable person, and I find that time flies when I’m with friends. That said, I do need some quiet time on my own now and then.

tip.ar: قارن بين الخيارين بوضوح.
tip.en: Compare the two options clearly.

qs.q: Is there a hobby you would like to try?
qs.model: I’d love to try scuba diving. The Red Sea has some of the best coral reefs in the world, and it seems a shame not to explore them when they’re so close.

tip.ar: استخدم I’d love to / I’ve always wanted to.
tip.en: Use I’d love to / I’ve always wanted to.

qs.q: Do you think people have enough free time nowadays?
qs.model: Not really. Most people are busier than ever, and even when they’re free, they’re often checking work messages on their phones, so they never fully switch off.

tip.ar: سؤال عام: تحدث عن الناس عمومًا لا عن نفسك فقط.
tip.en: General question: talk about people in general.

qs.q: What is your favourite food?
qs.model: I’d have to say kabsa. It’s a traditional rice dish with meat and spices, and my mother makes the best one I’ve ever tasted. We usually have it on Fridays with the whole family.

tip.ar: صف الطبق لشخص لا يعرفه.
tip.en: Describe the dish for someone who doesn’t know it.

qs.q: Do you like cooking?
qs.model: I’m not a great cook, to be honest, but I can make a few simple things like omelettes and pasta. I’d like to learn more before I go abroad to study.

tip.ar: الصراحة مقبولة: لا تحتاج أن تقول الحقيقة الكاملة، المهم لغة جيدة.
tip.en: Honesty is fine; what matters is good language.

qs.q: Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?
qs.model: At home, generally. Home-cooked food is healthier and cheaper, and it’s more relaxed. But eating out is nice for special occasions, like birthdays.

tip.ar: أعطِ سببين لتفضيلك.
tip.en: Give two reasons for your preference.

qs.q: Have people’s eating habits changed in your country?
qs.model: Yes, a lot. Fast food has become very popular, especially among young people, and that’s led to health problems. On the other hand, more people are now interested in healthy eating and going to the gym.

tip.ar: اذكر تغيرًا سلبيًا وآخر إيجابيًا لتظهر التوازن.
tip.en: Mention a negative and a positive change.

qs.q: What is the weather usually like where you live?
qs.model: It’s hot for most of the year. In summer, temperatures often go above forty-five degrees, so people stay indoors in the afternoon. Winter is much milder and really pleasant.

tip.ar: استخدم مفردات مثل mild، humid، scorching.
tip.en: Use words like mild, humid, scorching.

qs.q: What is your favourite season?
qs.model: Winter, without a doubt. The weather is perfect for spending time outdoors, and it’s the season for camping in the desert, which I absolutely love.

tip.ar: «without a doubt» تعبير قوي للتفضيل.
tip.en: “Without a doubt” is a strong preference phrase.

qs.q: Does the weather affect your mood?
qs.model: I think it does a little. When it’s extremely hot, I feel tired and less motivated, whereas a cool, sunny day puts me in a really good mood.

tip.ar: استخدم whereas للمقارنة.
tip.en: Use whereas to compare.

qs.q: Would you like to live in a place with a different climate?
qs.model: Maybe for a short time. I’d like to experience snow properly, but I think I’d miss the sunshine after a while.

tip.ar: «I think I’d miss…» استخدام صحيح للشرط.
tip.en: Conditional: “I think I’d miss…”.

vocab.en: puts me in a good mood

qs.q: Do you enjoy reading?
qs.model: Yes, but I don’t read as much as I used to. When I was at school, I read a lot of adventure novels, but now I mostly read articles online.

tip.ar: «not as much as I used to» مقارنة طبيعية بين الماضي والحاضر.
tip.en: “Not as much as I used to” contrasts past and present.

qs.q: What kind of books do you like?
qs.model: I’m really into biographies, especially of successful entrepreneurs. I find it inspiring to read about how people overcame difficulties to achieve their goals.

tip.ar: «I’m really into…» = أحب جدًا (عامية مقبولة).
tip.en: “I’m really into…” = I really like.

qs.q: Do you prefer paper books or e-books?
qs.model: Paper books, definitely. I spend all day looking at screens, so it’s nice to hold a real book. E-books are more convenient for travelling, though.

tip.ar: أضف «though» في النهاية لتضيف فكرة مقابلة.
tip.en: Add “though” at the end for a contrast.

qs.q: Do you think children read less these days?
qs.model: I’m afraid so. Children have so many other forms of entertainment, like video games and short videos, that reading can seem slow and boring to them.

tip.ar: «I’m afraid so» = نعم للأسف.
tip.en: “I’m afraid so” = unfortunately yes.

qs.q: How often do you use your phone?
qs.model: Far too often, to be honest. I use it for almost everything: studying, messaging, banking and entertainment. I sometimes try to put it away for an hour, but it’s hard.

tip.ar: «Far too often» تعبير طبيعي للمبالغة.
tip.en: “Far too often” is natural emphasis.

qs.q: What app do you use the most?
qs.model: Probably a messaging app. My family has a group chat, and we share news and photos all day long, so it’s a great way to stay in touch.

tip.ar: اشرح لماذا تستخدمه.
tip.en: Explain why you use it.

qs.q: Is there any technology you could not live without?
qs.model: I’d struggle without my laptop. All my university work is on it, and I use it to attend online lectures and to work on projects with my classmates.

tip.ar: «I’d struggle without» بديل لـ «I can’t live without».
tip.en: “I’d struggle without” instead of “I can’t live without”.

qs.q: Do older people in your family use technology?
qs.model: More than you’d expect. My grandmother has learned to make video calls, which means she can see her grandchildren who live in other cities. She’s become quite confident with it.

tip.ar: أعطِ مثالًا محددًا من حياتك.
tip.en: Give a specific example from your life.

qs.q: Do you have many friends?
qs.model: I have a lot of acquaintances, but only a few close friends. Most of them I’ve known since primary school, so we’re almost like brothers.

tip.ar: فرّق بين acquaintances وclose friends.
tip.en: Distinguish acquaintances and close friends.

qs.q: What do you usually do with your friends?
qs.model: We often meet at a café in the evening and just chat for hours. Sometimes we play football or go on a road trip during the holidays.

tip.ar: استخدم often/sometimes لوصف التكرار.
tip.en: Use frequency adverbs.

qs.q: What makes someone a good friend?
qs.model: I think loyalty is the most important thing. A good friend supports you when things go wrong, not only when everything is going well.

tip.ar: حدد صفة واشرحها بمثال.
tip.en: Pick one quality and explain it.

qs.q: Is it easy to make new friends as an adult?
qs.model: Not as easy as when you’re a child. Adults are busy with work and family, so there are fewer chances to meet people and build close relationships.

tip.ar: قارن بين الطفولة والبلوغ.
tip.en: Compare childhood and adulthood.
